You are an experienced JEE and NEET teacher. Solve the question below on your own.

You see only the question and its options. You do not see the answer key, the stored solution, or any student comment. Do not guess what the expected answer is. Work it out.

Rules:
- Write the working first, then the value, then the answer. Choose the status last, so it agrees with your working.
- Solve from first principles and check your arithmetic.
- If your value matches an option, the status is "solved" and the answer is that option, even if the question is worded loosely. Explain any wording problem in "note".
- If data needed to solve the question is missing, set "status" to "cannot_solve" and name the missing data in "note".
- If your result matches none of the options, set "status" to "no_option_matches" and give your result in "value".
- If more than one option is correct in a single-correct question, or none is, say so in "note".
- Answer format:
  - single-correct: one letter, for example "B"
  - multiple-correct: every correct letter, comma separated, for example "A, C, D"
  - integer: the number only, in the unit the question asks for, for example "8"
- "value": your final result with its unit, for example "50 V".
- "working": a short worked solution, at most 6 lines.
- "note": anything wrong or unclear in the question itself. Leave it empty if nothing is wrong.
request.user:
Subject: Physics
Question type: single-correct (exactly one option is right)

A glass tube of uniform internal radius (r) has a valve separating the two identical ends. Initially, the valve is in a tightly closed position. End 1 has a hemispherial soap bubble of radius r . End 2 has sub-hemispherical soap bubble as shown in figure.
Just after opening the valve.
(A) air from end 1 flows towards end 2 . No change in the volume of the soap bubbles
(B) air from end 1 flows towards end 2. Volume of the soap bubble at end 1 decreases
(C) no change occurs
(D) air from end 2 flows towards end 1 . Volume of the soap bubble at end 1 increases

result.working: Excess pressure inside a soap bubble is ΔP = 4T/R, where R is the radius of curvature. At a tube mouth of radius r, a hemispherical cap has the smallest possible radius of curvature, R = r. A sub-hemispherical cap has R > r. So the pressure at end 1 (4T/r) is greater than the pressure at end 2 (4T/R). When the valve opens, air flows from end 1 to end 2. Bubble 1 therefore shrinks and its volume decreases, while bubble 2 grows.
result.value: Air flows from end 1 to end 2; the volume of bubble 1 decreases
result.note: The figure is not shown. The answer assumes the usual figure, where end 2 carries a shallow cap (less than a hemisphere) whose radius of curvature is greater than r.
